title: Structured assertions for low-bandwidth SDKs: PRD sketch
summary: Sketch PRD for an assertion-first SDK surface that lets low-bandwidth and intermittent clients safely consume streaming/partial structured outputs and call tools while minimizing tokens and network roundtrips.
goals: Define a compact assertion envelope format that travels with incremental streaming frames and expresses validation semantics (required/optional/heuristic) without heavy schema payloads
Enable SDKs to verify partial structured outputs locally and decide: accept, request refinement, or call an external tool (explicit tool-call handoff) with minimal latency
Provide developer ergonomics: a tiny assertions API (<= 3 surface calls) that integrates in existing streaming callbacks and runs in constrained environments (mobile, edge nodes)
Design telemetry and failure modes so operators can attribute regressions to model drift, assertion mismatches, or network truncation
non_goals: Replacing full JSON Schema for general validation (we aim for compact assertion hints, not full schema validation runtime)
Shipping a complete server-side policy engine in this phase (we will recommend signatures/policies but not implement global enforcement)
Baking in a single serialization format for all partners — prefer a small portable envelope with versioning
success_metrics: Reduction in average bytes per session for mobile SDKs when using assertion envelopes vs naive full-schema validation (>35% target)
Decrease in developer time-to-integrate structured tool-calls in sample apps (target: <2 hours for basic flow)
False-positive assertion rate (assert that content is valid when it's not) below 1% on evaluation prompt set
Operator-visible classification of structured failures (model vs transport vs integration) for >= 90% of mismatch incidents
requirements: Compact assertion envelope: max 512 bytes typical, 2kB worst-case; carries assertion id, minimal hint tokens, version, confidence score
Frame-level assertions: every incremental streaming frame MAY include zero or more assertions that reference named output fields or offsets
Local SDK API: onAssertion(assertionEnvelope) -> {accept, refineRequest(reason), toolCall(toolSpec)}
Tool-call handoff contract: concise toolSpec references server-side tool id + optional client-provided context blob (prefetch-friendly, base64 small payloads)
Graceful degradation: when assertion cannot be evaluated locally, SDK requests a refinement stream (delta fetch) rather than full re-run
Telemetry labels: assertion_id, model_version, frame_offset, eval_outcome, client_eval_time_ms
Backward compatibility: assertion envelope must support a v1 -> v2 upgrade path so older SDKs ignore unknown hint types
Security: client context blobs are encrypted in transit and subject to same data retention rules as request payloads
acceptance_criteria: Reference mobile SDK integrates onAssertion and successfully triggers a mock tool call in a constrained network lab
Product playground ingest shows <512B typical per assertion envelope for 90% of sampled prompts
Telemetry pipeline surfaces first-class counters for: assertion_accepted, assertion_refined, assertion_tool_call, assertion_ignored
Playbook for engineers describing how to author assertion hints and test regressions is drafted and reviewed
constraints_and_assumptions: We assume streaming frames are delivered in-order for a session. Minimum viable assertion expressivity focuses on field-level presence/format and short enumerations; complex nested invariants will be out-of-scope for v1. Network budgets for target clients are ~50KB/session average (benchmark to validate).
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal experiment (SDK + runtime flag) with 3 mobile apps and one web client (4 weeks). Phase 1: limited beta with customers opt-in and telemetry collection (8 weeks). Phase 2: public docs, npm/pip release, and guardrail templates for common tool-call flows (4–6 weeks). Each phase gated on metrics above and 2-week stability window.
open_questions: What is the canonical compact representation? (binary CBOR-lite vs dense JSON with camelCase short keys)
How do we represent probabilistic assertions (confidence 0.7) and how should SDKs act on sub-threshold confidences?
Do we allow client-supplied assertion rewrites (developer can post-process assertion before evaluating)? Security/abuse implications?
Should the server offer precompiled assertion bundles for offline clients to reduce per-frame size?
implementation_notes: Start with a JSON-first v1 envelope using short keys (a, v, id, c, f, t) and instrument the runtime to emit assertion envelopes alongside frames. SDKs will implement a tiny verifier that matches simple regex enums and presence checks. Avoid heavyweight parsing in JS runtimes — provide native helpers for Android/iOS where possible.
notes: This doc is intentionally lightweight: aim to iterate quickly in the mobile lab and capture live examples. Produce a seeded prompt collection (50 prompts) that exercises presence/enum/format assertions and tooling handoffs. After Phase 0, reconcile with hosted-api streaming framing PRD and SDK ergonomics playbook.
